papers.title: Scaled boundary finite elements for FFT-based computational micromechanics
papers.abstract: We introduce a matrix-free FFT-based solver for three-dimensional linear elastic homogenization problems discretized by the scaled boundary finite element method (SBFEM) on a voxel grid. Owing to its analytical solution in the radial direction, the SBFEM discretization is inherently softer than fully integrated voxel finite elements, whereas its displacement-based formulation remains symmetric, conforming, and supports arbitrary stiffness anisotropy. These properties make SBFEM an attractive candidate for porous and highly heterogeneous microstructures, where existing voxel-based FFT discretizations offer no generally reliable choice: Reduced-integration hexahedral elements, equivalently the rotated staggered grid discretization, may suffer from hourglass instabilities in the presence of voids, whereas fully integrated hexahedral elements are often too stiff. The proposed discretization uses hexahedral SBFEM cells on the full voxel mesh of a regular periodic grid, retaining the simplicity of a fixed-resolution voxel representation without requiring adaptive mesh coarsening. The main contribution is a preconditioner based on the homogeneous SBFEM stiffness operator. We show that this preconditioner may be applied locally in Fourier space and that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by the material contrast, independently of the grid resolution. This result enables a fully matrix-free implementation of the SBFEM-discretized problem, without assembling or storing the global stiffness matrix. Numerical experiments on a short-fibre reinforced composite, a polyurethane foam and a sand-based binder jet microstructure demonstrate robust convergence and competitive accuracy compared with established voxel discretizations. In particular, SBFEM remains stable for porous microstructures, for which reduced-integration hexahedral elements become unstable.

papers.title: Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors
papers.abstract: Pretraining an encoder once and reusing it across tasks is a widespread approach in vision and language. However, neural symbolic mathematics still trains a dedicated sequence-to-sequence model for each task, so that no representation of a function is shared. In this work, we propose the Function Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Func-JEPA, abbreviated f-JEPA): an encoder of mathematical functions, pretrained on their symbolic form, whose latent space imitates the Sobolev space H^1 and in which differentiation is a learned latent operator. The norm of a latent is computed exactly from the function, whereas its direction is learned to match Sobolev angles. The frozen encoder is then reused by lightweight modules for decoding, composition, integration, and regression from samples. The representation and four downstream tasks are evaluated within and outside the pretraining distribution. f-JEPA recovers exact formulas from noisy samples more often than the compared symbolic-regression methods, whereas computer algebra and task-specific models remain stronger on standard integration and differential-equation benchmarks.

papers.title: In-Context Estimation and Prediction for Parametric ODEs
papers.abstract: Transformers have demonstrated the ability to perform in-context learning, that is, to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without updating their parameters. Existing theory has largely focused on emulating gradient-based algorithms for convex statistical problems or establishing general function approximation guarantees without exploiting the underlying statistical structure. We study in-context parameter estimation and trajectory prediction for parametric ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where estimation is generally nonconvex. Under suitable identifiability and regularity conditions, we construct a transformer that estimates unknown system parameters from noisy trajectory observations through a two-stage approximate maximum likelihood procedure: a coarse search provides an initialization within a locally strongly convex region, followed by gradient descent with local linear contraction. For prediction, we compose this estimator with a neural approximation of the ODE solution map. We further show that, through parameter sharing, a single transformer can perform both parameter estimation and trajectory prediction simultaneously. For these constructions, we establish nonasymptotic guarantees and finite-pretraining oracle inequalities that separate errors due to finite pretraining data, finite context length, and finite-sized transformer approximation. Numerical experiments on linear and nonlinear ODEs further show that pretrained transformers can benefit from longer inference contexts without updating their weights.

papers.title: Two-Sided Projection-Based Model Reduction of Parametric Generalized Algebraic Riccati Equations via Grassmann-Manifold Optimization
papers.abstract: Parametric generalized algebraic Riccati equations arise in many-query problems in optimal control, state estimation, and filtering, where repeated full-order solutions may become computationally prohibitive for large-scale systems. In this paper, within a projection-based model reduction framework, we propose a two-sided projection approach that constructs reduced bases by minimizing the aggregate relative two-sided projection error of Riccati solution snapshots. Under suitable dissipativity assumptions, the resulting Galerkin-projected PGARE admits a unique symmetric positive semidefinite stabilizing solution. For error assessment, we employ an existing residual-based a posteriori error estimator for the full-order Riccati residual. A projection-based error decomposition developed in this work provides the theoretical motivation for the proposed basis construction. To accommodate clustered solution manifolds, we extend the framework to localized model reduction by combining parameter-space proximity and solution-space correlation for clustering, with classifier-based online basis selection. Numerical experiments on parameterized heat-conduction problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed global and localized approaches in terms of approximation accuracy and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Global Lanczos with stochastic error correction for trace estimation of matrix functions
papers.abstract: We propose a new method for computing the trace of a matrix function $f(A)$, where $A$ is a large, sparse, symmetric matrix. Our approach combines a deterministic global Lanczos approximation with a stochastic correction of its error. Starting the global Lanczos process with the identity matrix yields a direct approximation of the trace through a small tridiagonal matrix. The resulting basis matrices are polynomials in $A$, allowing the process to be implemented using sparse matrix-matrix multiplications when low-degree polynomials in $A$ have moderate fill-in. However, increased fill-in may limit the number of iterations that can be performed efficiently. To address this limitation, we derive an exact representation of the global Lanczos error as the trace of a matrix function and apply a stochastic estimator to the remainder. Even a moderately accurate estimate can substantially improve the accuracy, combining the deterministic method with the rapid initial convergence of stochastic trace estimators. We discuss error bounds and variance reduction, and present numerical experiments that compare the resulting method with existing ones.

papers.title: Spectral Conditioning of Weighted Multivariate Vandermonde Operators via Radial Beurling--Selberg Approximation
papers.abstract: We establish explicit eigenvalue bounds for Gram matrices of weighted multivariate Vandermonde operators with separated nodes on a torus. The squared magnitudes of the weights are samples of a nonnegative radial spectral energy density whose profile has bounded variation, finite energy, and finite weighted variation cost; compact support is not required. The estimate holds in every dimension and depends on the periodic Euclidean separation and the weighted variation integral. For compactly supported profiles, our analysis combines a signed layer decomposition with the ball approximants of Holt and Vaaler; the noncompactly supported case follows by truncation. Combining the resulting radial envelopes with a bandlimited sampling identity based on Poisson summation yields the spectral bounds by eliminating off-diagonal interactions and nonzero diagonal aliases. The result covers nonmonotone profiles and discontinuous radial low-pass filters, and it is complemented by a global elementary upper bound on the Holt--Vaaler cost that exhibits two radial regimes.

papers.title: NeRI: Neural Residual Iteration for Elliptic Operator Equations and Variational Inequalities
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a so-called {\it Neural Residual Iteration} (NeRI), a weak-form neural-network framework for solving a class of elliptic operator equations and variational inequalities, including nonlinear and nonsymmetric problems that may not admit a global energy functional. The key idea is to construct, at each iteration, a state-dependent linear functional whose derivative with respect to the trial function recovers the current weak residual. A single gradient step is then performed on the residual, yielding a residual-driven neural update without requiring a global energy functional or an additional test network. From a function-space perspective, NeRI can be interpreted as a neural-tangent-kernel-preconditioned realization of classical residual iterations, thereby bridging classical iterative solvers and neural-network optimization. We further extend NeRI to elliptic variational inequalities (VIs) through penalized and constraint-preserving formulations. For wide two-layer networks under gradient flow, we prove finite-time lazy-training estimates and derive an $H^1$-error decomposition relative to the exact weak solution. Numerical experiments on several elliptic problems demonstrate the effectiveness of NeRI, particularly for nonsymmetric and low-regularity problems.

papers.title: Delay Closure of Observable Dynamics for the Heat Equation
papers.abstract: We study finite-delay representations of point observables, which are solution values at selected spatial locations, for spatially discretized heat equations. We show that the observables satisfy closed dynamical systems whose evolution depends only on their own history, without requiring solution values elsewhere in the domain. Using semigroup properties, we analyze low-rank approximate closures that can use substantially fewer delay terms than the exact representation. We consider two computational approaches: direct least-squares fitting of delay coefficients from observable trajectories and shift-invert Krylov approximation of the semigroup using preconditioned linear solves. Numerical experiments for constant- and variable-coefficient heat equations in one, two, and three dimensions illustrate the effects of memory length and sensor information on prediction. The results are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Pole rigidity in root-optimal rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
papers.abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than $\pi$, the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many $\varphi$-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.

papers.title: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
papers.abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $\rho_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_t\rho=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2\rho)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/\rho$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $\Gamma$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

papers.title: Spectral Gaps and Low-Energy Modes in Anisotropic High-Contrast PDEs
papers.abstract: We study the low-energy spectrum of high-contrast partial differential equations with strongly anisotropic inclusions. The inclusion stiffness and mass are scaled by a contrast parameter \(\eta\), while a small material eigenvalue \(\epsilon\) controls anisotropy. Stable extensions of local kernel fields give eigenvalue upper bounds proportional to the inverse contrast, uniformly in anisotropy. Additional low-energy modes arise from fields whose nonzero differential images lie in weak material directions. Each fixed family of compatible weak fields yields additional eigenvalue upper bounds of order $\epsilon+ \eta^{-1}$, provided a stable extension exists. Under discrete stability assumptions, we obtain corresponding finite element bounds for the weak modes represented by the mesh. For separable scalar diffusion, we prove norm-resolvent convergence to independent background Dirichlet and inclusion Neumann operators as contrast tends to infinity with anisotropy fixed. Numerical experiments for four PDE models illustrate weak modes and mesh-dependent spectral transitions, and scalar diffusion experiments also test spectral decoupling and eigenvalue counting.

papers.title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
papers.abstract: We propose, analyze, and implement a convolution quadrature (CQ) algorithm for transient acoustic waves in an unbounded medium consisting of a heterogeneous domain embedded in free space, where the wave speed may be spatially variable and discontinuous. Multistep CQ, applied to the time-domain solution operator, reduces the evolution problem to a family of Helmholtz problems with damped complex frequencies, which can be solved independently in parallel, all time steps at once. The frequency problems are discretized by an overlapping coupling of finite elements (FEM) on a polygonal/polyhedral domain containing the inhomogeneity, and boundary elements (BEM) on a smooth curve enclosed by that domain, in the region where the medium is homogeneous, which accounts exactly for the unbounded exterior. Neither discretization needs to conform to the geometry of the heterogeneous domain, nor to each other. For the resulting FEM--BEM coupling we prove bounds for the solution operators of the transformed problems that are explicit in the Laplace parameter and the wave speed. These bounds yield convergence of the time discretization for A-stable multistep schemes. We also prove explicit estimates on the exponential decay of the transformed solutions away from the heterogeneity, which show that the correction provided by the BEM part is small but relevant, and cheap to compute: a few GMRES iterations suffice, and the correction is needed only over a fixed range of weakly damped frequencies, beyond which it becomes negligible and can be dropped. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates in time and space and explore iterative (multigrid) methods for the interior FEM problems.

papers.title: Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Stationary Convective Brinkman--Forchheimer Extended Darcy Equations with a Nonlinear Slip Boundary Condition of Friction Type
papers.abstract: This work develops and analyzes several discontinuous Galerkin methods for a variational inequality associated with the stationary convective Brinkman--Forchheimer extended Darcy (CBFeD) system. The CBFeD model generalizes the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations by incorporating additional damping and pumping terms. The resulting variational inequality characterizes the motion of a viscous, incompressible fluid in a saturated porous medium under a friction-type slip boundary condition. For the CBFeD variational inequality, we first explore the existence of a unique weak solution. Then, we establish the existence, uniqueness, and stability of the numerical solutions obtained using discontinuous Galerkin methods. Optimal error estimates are derived, measured in the broken $H^1$-norm for the velocity and in the $L^2$-norm for the pressure, when linear velocity elements and piecewise constant pressure approximations are employed. Numerical simulations are carried out to confirm the theoretically predicted convergence orders and to highlight key strengths of the method, including its ability to capture discontinuities, effectively resolve shear layers, handle advection-dominated regimes, and operate robustly on general polygonal meshes.

papers.title: First-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise
papers.abstract: We prove first-order convergence of finite-difference approximations to the Freidlin--Wentzell minimum action for diffusions with multiplicative noise, which answers the question of the sharp rate left open in [Hong, Jin, Sheng, \emph{IMA J. Numer. Anal.} 45 (2025), 1501--1536]. As shown in that work, a bound on the action controls only the $L^2$ norm of the velocity, which leads to a half-order estimate for the difference between the discrete and continuous actions. To improve it, we use the discrete Euler--Lagrange equation to derive mesh-independent $L^\infty$ bounds on the velocity of piecewise affine interpolants of stationary discrete paths with bounded action. For the case of a unique continuous minimizer, we identify the leading coefficient of the error between the discrete and continuous minimum actions on uniform grids, and a scalar example shows that the first-order error bound is sharp. We also prove strong $H^1(0,T;\mathbb R^d)$ subsequential convergence of interpolated discrete minimizers. Numerical experiments for a two-protein genetic toggle switch confirm first-order convergence of the discrete action for transitions in both directions.

papers.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
papers.abstract: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $\nu>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

papers.title: Explicit Regularization for Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Learning the underlying probability distribution from samples is a core problem in statistics and applied mathematics. Generative models based on diffusion and flow matching learn a velocity field whose flow transports a known distribution to the data distribution. They produce novel, realistic samples, although the empirical learning problem is ill posed near the data distribution. Its minimizer transports the samples onto the training data, and small perturbations of the data change the velocity field strongly near the end of the flow. The observed generalization is often attributed to implicit regularization by the network parameterization, early stopping of the training, and the time integration during sampling. Explicit regularization has advanced the theory and computation of many inverse problems and has recently been proposed to prevent memorization in generative models. With a regularizer on the magnitude of the velocity, however, the field approaches the memorizing velocity unless the regularization parameter grows to infinity fast enough, and it then stays bounded by a constant that is small only for large parameters. We show that penalizing the derivatives of order $k$ of the velocity renders the $D$-dimensional empirical problem well posed uniformly in time if $2k > D$ and the training points are in general position. Our experiments in one and two dimensions discretize the velocity with splines and use direct solvers for the regularized least-squares problems to exclude optimization error. Refining the discretization in space and time changes the error of the Hessian-regularized flows only marginally, whereas without the regularizer the error tends to that of memorization. These flows generalize, with errors comparable to or lower than those of well-tuned kernel density estimates.

papers.title: Adaptive Precision Cholesky with Error Guarantees
papers.abstract: Modern accelerators increasingly support low-precision formats such as 8-bit floats and integers to speed up machine learning. We show that a Cholesky factorization in which both GEMM and TRSM are implemented using the fixed-point Ozaki 1 scheme satisfies the same backward error bounds as the standard floating-point Cholesky factorization, and that the same holds for a Cholesky factorization computed using a low-precision MicroScaled GEMM. We then use our error analyses to construct an adaptive precision Cholesky factorization that exploits low-precision formats while respecting a prescribed element-wise error bound, as long as the factorization succeeds. We test it in two settings. First, we use it to choose the number of Ozaki 1 slices at each iteration, with SYRK/GEMM and TRSM emulated in INT8 fixed-point arithmetic to attain double-precision accuracy. Second, we use it to build a low-precision Cholesky preconditioner for the conjugate gradient method (PCG), in which SYRK/GEMM take low-precision inputs and accumulate in high precision, with the input format selected adaptively for each panel; if the factorization breaks down, diagonal perturbation still yields a valid preconditioner, at the cost of the error bound guarantees. On an NVIDIA GH200, the adaptive Ozaki 1-based factorization is up to 29% faster than a right-looking Cholesky using a fixed slice count of 7, and up to 69% faster than one using cuBLAS' Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP), while maintaining the same error guarantees. For PCG, FP8 factorizations with diagonal perturbation form effective preconditioners on the 13 tested SuiteSparse matrices, reducing the number of PCG iterations by up to $12\times$ over CG on the same matrix diagonally scaled by powers of two. For synthetic matrices with arithmetic spectra, and geometric spectra with $\kappa \le 10^4$, FP8 preconditioners also reduce the number of CG iterations.

papers.title: SPIKE-Accelerated Split-Bregman/ADMM Methods for Obstacle Problems and American Option Pricing under Jump-Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: This paper presents a parallel split Bregman/alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) \cite{goldstein,tran} for obstacle problems and for the linear complementarity problems (LCPs) that arise in the pricing of American options under the Black--Scholes and Merton jump-diffusion \cite{merton} models. The auxiliary variable of ADMM decouples the inequality constraint from the differential operator, so that every iteration consists of a linear solve with a fixed banded matrix and a pointwise projection. The matrix is factorized once by the SPIKE algorithm \cite{spike}, as in the parallel direct approach of \cite{singh}, and reused in all iterations and time steps in a Fortran~90 MPI implementation. Convergence is proved by a Lyapunov functional for every positive augmentation parameter, for the symmetric obstacle problem and the non-symmetric option LCP alike, and the iterates do not depend on the number of processes. The method therefore needs a single factorization, no tuned relaxation parameter and only pointwise, perfectly parallel updates. One- and two-dimensional obstacle problems, the Black--Scholes call and American put, and European and American options under Merton's model are computed and compared with exact, closed-form, binomial and published values. In two dimension a speed-up of $3.92$ on four processes is obtained. It is also shown that the augmentation parameter has to be scaled to the diagonal of the time-stepping matrix when only a few inner iterations are used.

papers.title: Efficient Recursive Evaluation of Gaussian, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian Tail Probabilities
papers.abstract: Accurate computation of tail probabilities motivates efficient high-order implementations of the $G_n^{(1)}$ extrapolation transformation. We derive finite recurrence relations in the transformation order for Gaussian, gamma, and inverse Gaussian tail approximations. The Gaussian and inverse Gaussian numerator and denominator sequences satisfy four-term recurrences, whereas the gamma sequences satisfy a three-term recurrence. The derivation exploits the structure of the underlying differential operator and shows that the reduced numerator and denominator obey recurrences with identical coefficients. This construction avoids the repeated evaluation of higher-order derivatives and nested sums required by the explicit formulations. As a result, generating the approximation sequence through order $n$ requires $O(n)$ arithmetic operations, compared with $O(n^3)$ for the Gaussian and gamma distributions and $O(n^4)$ for the inverse Gaussian distribution. The recurrence algorithms also require only a fixed number of previously computed quantities at each order. Numerical results for the three distributions are in excellent agreement with values reported in the literature

papers.title: Explicit geometric integrators for Langevin equations with superquadratic potentials
papers.abstract: We propose a new class of explicit methods for Langevin equations with a superquadratic potential that simultaneously preserve the conformal symplecticity and ergodicity as well as achieving high-order convergence. The construction is based on a mollified potential approach, in which the original potential is truncated to quadratic growth at infinity and globally mollified to control the superquadratic behavior while maintaining the underlying properties of the original dynamics. By appropriately choosing the cut-off radius, the far-field quadratic coefficient, and the step size, we obtain the coercivity of the mollified potential and derive its derivative estimates. These estimates allow us to prove uniform-in-time weak convergence for the proposed (including higher-order) explicit conformal symplectic numerical methods. Since the mollified potential is identical to the original one in a ball whose radius grows as the step size decreases, the computational cost of the new methods is essentially the same as that of the usual schemes (e.g., BAOAB) applied to the original potential. Numerical experiments are provided to illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Barron Approximation and locally optimal weight densities for shallow neural networks
papers.abstract: Mean field theories provide optimization results for shallow neural networks by analyzing the weight distribution in infinite width limits. Corresponding results for finite sized networks are obtained by particle approximations, for which sharp quantitative bounds are still an open problem. In this paper, we consider a modified mean field loss, which allows a more fine grained control over finite sized networks. We prove convexity and equidistribution properties, which directly lead to Barron type approximation results for networks sampled from local loss minimizers. We demonstrate that particle approximations of the new loss function naturally lead to gradient descent methods with dropout type regularization.

papers.title: Enhancing Exploration in Ensemble Kalman Inversion via Covariance Inflation and Projected Dropout
papers.abstract: Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) is a derivative-free and parallelizable method for parameter estimation in Bayesian inverse problems involving expensive forward models. It adapts Kalman filtering by repeatedly assimilating the observation data through an artificial dynamical system with identity state evolution and the parameter-to-observation map as its observation operator. However, its performance can be limited by ensemble collapse and confinement to the affine span of the initial ensemble. We propose an exploration-enhanced EKI framework that combines multiplicative covariance inflation with a projected-dropout correction of the ensemble mean. Inflation helps maintain ensemble spread, while projected dropout enables the mean to explore directions beyond the initial affine span. For linear inverse problems, we provide a discrete-time, finite-ensemble analysis of the resulting method and prove the least-squares objective converges exponentially to its minimum in expectation. Within the initial ensemble subspace, the contraction factor is independent of the conditioning of the inverse problem, and the limiting ensemble covariance provides a low-rank representation of the posterior covariance. Experiments on ill-conditioned linear systems, 100-dimensional nonlinear benchmarks, and a PDE-constrained barotropic flow inverse problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Variance Stable Gaussian Smoothing Estimator for Arbitrary High-order Derivatives
papers.abstract: Computing high-order partial derivatives in high dimensions by automatic differentiation can be costly in both computation and memory. Stein's identity offers an alternative through Gaussian smoothing, but the variance of the resulting estimators can diverge as the step size tends to zero, even with antithetic sampling. We propose a variance stabilization technique that extends antithetic sampling from a reflection pair to $n$ equally spaced points on a circle in the complex plane. Under local analyticity, we prove that, when $n$ is at least the derivative order, the bias is of order $O(\sigma^n)$ and the variance remains bounded as the smoothing step size $\sigma$ tends to zero. Numerical experiments support these predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the estimator in physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for polyharmonic and Cahn--Hilliard equations. The technique mitigates the bias-variance trade-off in smoothing-based derivative estimation and is useful for PINNs solving high-order partial differential equations.

papers.title: A new formula for Moore-Penrose inverses of rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new formula for the Moore-Penrose inverses of the rank-deficient Toeplitz matrices, based on the quasi-direct decompositions of Toeplitz matrices. Numerical examples are presented to verify the validity and the efficiency of our method.

papers.title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
papers.abstract: Harvest quadrature can change a discrete optimal control problem even when the state scheme stays fixed. We study this effect for a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. The difference appears in a model with harvesting alone: rewarding the scheme's removal flux gives a strictly convex reduced cost, whereas using prey density at the start of each step overestimates harvest and can create negative curvature and a strict local minimum that is not global. Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(\tau)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $\tau$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

papers.title: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
papers.abstract: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

papers.title: Discontinuity-Aware Solvers for Vapor-Compression Cycles
papers.abstract: Physics-based models of vapor-compression cycles are often formulated as large, stiff DAE systems with derivative discontinuities introduced at the points of phase change. We use an implementation of a discontinuity-aware ODE and DAE solver scheme that uses domain-specific, user-declared information to compute appropriate time steps for more efficient integration. This scheme is made open-source within DifferentialEquations.jl. We demonstrate how discontinuity information can be specified symbolically in a declarative modeling language such as Dyad and passed to the solver to address the numerical challenges posed. We apply this discontinuity-aware technique to two applications: first, a scalar ODE with two discontinuities, and then a model of a full vapor-compression cycle. The discontinuity-aware solver yields significantly fewer step rejections and improved solver times, particularly with the Rodas5P solver at loose tolerances, as compared to standard error control, suggesting that exposing physical discontinuity information from equation-oriented models to adaptive solvers can improve practical simulation performance without requiring reassembly of the model.

papers.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
papers.abstract: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nystr\"om trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

papers.title: A bound-preserving hybrid lattice Boltzmann method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: Solutions to scalar hyperbolic conservation laws may develop discontinuities within finite time even from smooth initial data, while higher-order lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods tend to generate non-physical oscillations and out-of-bounds behavior near steep gradients. To address this issue, we first construct a first-order LB method with the upwind-type equilibrium distribution functions under the \(DdQ(2d+1)\) lattice structure, and establish its bound-preserving (BP) conditions. We then develop a second-order multiple-relaxation-time LB (MRT-LB) method by introducing the auxiliary source distribution functions, and analyze its \(L^2\) stability. Building on these, we propose a hybrid LB method that preserves the collision-streaming structure, by conservatively mixing first- and second-order updates through a convex constraint mechanism. We further establish the global BP (GBP), local BP (LBP), and relaxed LBP (RLBP) limiters in the hybrid LB method, together with the associated macroscopic BP constraints. Numerical experiments examine the convergence order, interface capturing performance, and discontinuity resolution capability of the proposed BP hybrid LB method. The results indicate that it effectively suppresses out-of-bounds behavior in the second-order LB method and reduces numerical dissipation in the first-order LB method, while maintaining the prescribed bounds and discrete mass conservation.

papers.title: Hyperspectral imaging from diffractograms
papers.abstract: We consider an optical system with a periodic point spread function, such as a camera with a periodic diffractive filter array placed near the sensor. Such systems produce a monochrome image that we call ``diffractogram'', and that multiplexes the spatial and spectral information about the scene. We present a method to efficiently invert this forward model and recover the hyperspectral scene. The inverse problem is formulated as a large scale $\ell_1$-penalized least squares problem that is solved iteratively with the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). A Krylov subspace solver, such as LSQR, may require tens to hundreds of iterations to approximatively solve the augmented least-squares problem required in each ADMM iteration. Here we present an exact direct solver for the augmented least-squares problems that exploits the periodicity of the point spread function. Each direct solve costs roughly as much as three LSQR iterations, eliminating inner iterations entirely. We validate the method on both synthetic and experimental datasets.
